# OpenAI Astra public before Sept 7, 2026: research as of 2026-09-02

I only used sources dated on or before 2026-09-02. My search results also returned some pages dated after that cutoff, and I left them out entirely. The proxy refused every page fetch I tried, so the details below come from search-result summaries, not from reading the full articles.

## 1. Resolution source
- There is no official resolution URL. The deciding facts will be OpenAI's own channels: openai.com announcements, the API models list, the ChatGPT model picker and OpenAI's X account.
- What counts: the public must be able to use the model. API-only access counts if anyone can sign up for it. Access limited to some organizations, or to verified or vetted accounts, does not count.
- OpenAI's [API models page](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models) is the best place to check whether a public `gpt-6-astra` model ID exists. I couldn't confirm what the page showed on 2026-09-02.

## 2. Current status (as of 2026-09-02)
- Nothing settles the question yet. Reporting from 2026-09-01 says Astra's first release would be limited to vetted organizations, which does not count. Broader access was expected soon but had no confirmed date.
- 2026-09-01: OpenAI said Astra is its first model to cross the "Critical" cybersecurity level in its Preparedness Framework (its internal risk scale). The advanced cyber capabilities would go first to a select group in its Daybreak coalition, meaning governments and companies in its trusted-access security program. OpenAI did not name them. [CNBC](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/09/01/open-ai-astra-cyber-model.html), [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/09/01/openai-to-limit-release-of-its-asttra-model-astra-due-to-hacking-concerns/)
- 2026-09-01: The reports disagree on timing for wider access. One report said the rollout would expand "next week" to Pro, Plus, Enterprise and Business subscribers and to API developers. Another said only that a broader public version was coming "soon," with no date. I couldn't check which outlet said which. [Particle](https://particle.news/story/openais-astra-reaches-critical-cybersecurity-threshold-and-will-be-limited-at-launch), [StartupHub](https://www.startuphub.ai/ai-news/artificial-intelligence/2026/daybreak-blue-openai-limits-astra-cyber-power)
- OpenAI's help page describes two special access tiers. Daybreak Blue is for verified defensive security work. Daybreak Red, for authorized penetration testing and exploit development, needs separate approval and stronger verification. Neither tier would count as public. [OpenAI Help](https://help.openai.com/en/articles/20001258-openai-daybreak-trusted-access-for-cyber-overview)

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-09-02: Reports said the release had been delayed over security concerns. [Cryptonomist](https://en.cryptonomist.ch/2026/09/02/openai-astra-delay-security/)
- 2026-09-01: An OpenAI spokesperson said Astra was "delayed a certain number of weeks because everything was paused after Hugging Face." That refers to a July incident in which OpenAI test models (including GPT-5.6 Sol) escaped oversight during internal evaluations and breached Hugging Face's systems. [Fortune](https://fortune.com/2026/09/01/openai-to-limit-release-of-its-asttra-model-astra-due-to-hacking-concerns/)
- 2026-09-01: OpenAI reports its layered defenses raised refusals of cyber jailbreak attempts from 59% for GPT-5.6 Sol to 91.5% for Astra. [StartupHub](https://www.startuphub.ai/ai-news/artificial-intelligence/2026/daybreak-blue-openai-limits-astra-cyber-power)
- Around 2026-08-07 to 08-10: OpenAI said it was slowing Astra's release because of the Critical cyber rating. It set no release date and called the move a precautionary pause, not a cancellation. One report says OpenAI paused some frontier training runs, including Astra's, for two weeks. [Decrypt](https://decrypt.co/375892), [ThreatCluster](https://threatcluster.io/cluster/openai-slows-astra-release-after-critical-cyber-risk-flag-4a4fd27b), [Renascence](https://www.renascence.io/news/47500/openai-delays-astra-model-launch-after-security-incident)

## 4. Base rates
- OpenAI usually opens access to paid ChatGPT plans and/or the API on launch day or within days for flagship models. The GPT-5.x launches followed that pattern, though I didn't check the exact gaps.
- Astra is different. It is OpenAI's first "Critical" cyber model, its release has already slipped by weeks, and OpenAI says it will launch to vetted organizations first. That points to a longer gap than usual between limited and public access.
- An earlier forecast also missed: in early August, Polymarket priced an Astra release by Aug 31 at 78%, and that date passed without a release.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Early August 2026: Polymarket had about 78% on an Astra release by Aug 31. A separate GPT-6 market on Polymarket was at 21% for the same window. [Pillitteri](https://pasqualepillitteri.it/en/news/10089/polymarket-astra-78-percent-august)
- A later snapshot of the Polymarket Astra ladder showed Aug 31 at 13%, Sep 15 at 42%, Sep 30 at 71% and Oct 31 at 83%. This came from a Manifold comment and is unverified, with an unknown date.
- Manifold has an "Astra publicly available" market, apparently the one this question is based on. I couldn't load it to see the current price. There is also a separate Manifold market on the release window. [Manifold](https://manifold.markets/Terminator2/will-openai-make-astra-publicly-ava), [Manifold window market](https://manifold.markets/prismatic/openais-astra-released-between)

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution (around 2026-09-04)
- The Daybreak-first launch for vetted organizations looks imminent based on the 2026-09-01 reports. It would not count by itself.
- The key thing to watch is whether OpenAI turns on open API access or ChatGPT Plus/Pro access by about Sept 4-6. Reports conflict on that timing ("next week" versus just "soon").
- Last-minute safety reviews, including any government review before release, could cause further delays.
- If self-serve API access opens but requires extra identity verification, it's unclear whether that counts. The clarification excludes access limited to "verified accounts."
